title: Capacity and Latency Budget Modeling
objective: Build a back-of-envelope capacity model with stated formulas and assumptions, allocate a latency budget across components, and identify the most likely bottleneck with supporting evidence.
whyThisMatters: Scaling decisions made on intuition alone are frequently wrong in the specific direction that costs the most. A capacity model that shows its formulas can be checked and corrected; a gut feeling about where the bottleneck will be cannot.
evidence: A capacity model document showing the formulas and input assumptions used, not just final numbers
A latency budget table allocating the end-to-end target across at least three components
A note identifying the single most likely bottleneck and the specific number from the model that points to it
acceptanceCriteria: Every capacity number states its formula and input assumptions, not a bare final figure.
The latency budget across components sums to no more than the stated end-to-end target.
The identified bottleneck is supported by a specific number from the model, not a general intuition.
